upheld.reason: This counterexample fixes F:R to R, F(x)=x cubed, so n=1 satisfies the supplier n>=1 hypothesis. The quantification over every epsilon concerns scalar stability balls, not a variable dimension; steps 1.2–3.1 use only that fixed line.

The state domain here is the whole line R, so every closed finite-radius ball about zero is contained in U, as required by the cited definition. The universal epsilon in L1 is valid for this fixed n=1 domain and does not generalize the source dimension.

The citing Statement already fixes n>=1 and F of class C^2 on the given open U. F2 uses the cylinder estimate only in this fixed dimension; its every-initial-value-problem clause cites the distinct maximal-ODE supplier and does not quantify over n.
